{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABcnfGNQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhGJyIQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 85, "title": "Derive the public animation timeline and playback end from each selected VMD duration (remove hardcoded 10 seconds)", "body": "## Problem

The public MMD/glTF comparison still exposes a hardcoded **10-second** time range in initial HTML and several browser tests, even though it already records and loads a per-motion `duration`. Playback/timeline labels should always reflect the **currently selected VMD's real duration**, not a fixed example length. The user specifically requested that animation length come from the animation data.

**Source distinction:** This is primarily a **duration consistency and regression-proofing fix**; do not incorrectly claim that the current runtime always plays exactly 10 seconds. In current `examples/main.ts`, runtime duration is already assigned from the selected retained VMD player and `timeline.max` is changed on selection. Nevertheless `examples/index.html` starts with `max="10"` and `0.00 / 10.00 s`, and some browser tests assume 10 seconds for every motion. Verify behavior end to end, including initial load, fast switching, and boundaries.

## Exact current locations (main d1958dcc3c1666d4e5116c5f3a7461de1059a485)

- [`examples/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/index.html): `#comparison-time` defaults to `max="10"`; `#comparison-time-label` starts `0.00 / 10.00 s`. These fixed defaults can be misleading during loading/Rest and fragile if real duration changes.
- [`tools/audit-public-motions.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/audit-public-motions.ts): `auditMotion(...).duration` currently computes `max(frame / 30)` over bone, morph and display records. Inspect consistency with the project's [`vmdDuration`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/packages/mmd-vmd/reader.ts) semantics, which include other retained sections as well, and decide one explicit, source-faithful rule. Do not trim valid source keys purely to shorten playback. Preserve unbound and retained source data.
- [`tools/public-motion.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/public-motion.ts): serializes `duration: motion.audit.duration` into each public `motion*.json`.
- [`packages/mmd-vmd/index.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/packages/mmd-vmd/index.ts) and [`packages/three-mmd-vmd/index.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/packages/three-mmd-vmd/index.ts): bound VMD duration and retained-player clamping/looping. Avoid unnecessary changes to these correct playback contracts.
- [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts): metadata includes `duration:number` (~line 147); it validates the selected player against metadata, sets `duration=activePlayers[0].duration` (~306), writes `timeline.max=String(duration)` at motion selection (~515) and initialization (~526), uses duration for on-screen time labels (~398), seek clamping (~472), end-of-play and loop (~523, ~580–581). Preserve this as the single authoritative duration through all controls.
- [`tests/browser/public-motion.spec.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tests/browser/public-motion.spec.ts): uses `seek(9.9)`, waits for `time===10` and assumes a loop wraps below 9 seconds.
- [`tests/browser/body-motion.spec.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tests/browser/body-motion.spec.ts): same `9.9` / `10` assumptions for body clips. Check any other fixed 10-second expectations throughout public playback/Physics tests; distinguish genuine fixture-specific constants from public-VMD assumptions.
- [`docs/public-motion.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion.md): document the public timeline contract and duration provenance accurately.

## Implementation requirements

- [ ] Establish a documented, unambiguous **source duration** policy: for a VMD this is derived from its last relevant retained keyframe(s) at the VMD 30 fps timebase, or the already validated canonical retained player's `duration`. Reconcile any mismatch between `auditMotion`, `vmdDuration`, metadata and retained player; do not derive duration from an arbitrary playback UI constant, the approximate Three.js mixer track alone, or the number of *visible* bound tracks. If an outermost retained key has no visible effect, do not silently drop it; document rather than changing source semantics.
- [ ] For each Uka and Gene Light clip (official sample, Laugh, Apology), confirm actual metadata duration, retained-player duration, reference clip duration and any relevant VMD source last frame; preserve correct clip identity and supported 1/30-frame time semantics. Verify the values are equal under the intended rule or report and fix any demonstrated mismatch.
- [ ] Replace hardcoded initial `max="10"` and `0.00 / 10.00 s` with an honest disabled/loading placeholder until metadata/player validation completes. Do not present a fabricated 10-second length for Rest/manual mode; specify simple behavior (disabled playback/slider and no misleading total time) for Rest.
- [ ] On initial load and every clip/model switch, set **one authoritative duration** for HTML slider `max`, displayed current/total seconds, playback/Restart/Loop behavior, active-player clamp and playback state. Preserve existing time state semantics: new motion starts at 0, play is disabled in Rest, changes update instantly without reloading the model or creating another renderer. Avoid stale displays from async loads and switching.
- [ ] Handle fractional `frame / 30` durations cleanly: final frame must be reachable, the slider must not skip the real endpoint due to `step` mismatch/rounding, and the label must be readable without claiming an exact integral number of seconds. Explicitly test zero or near-zero valid duration, noninteger last frames, and varying lengths; do not introduce divide-by-zero loops or stuck Play/Pause.
- [ ] When looping is off, playback stops **exactly at the selected clip's end** and leaves the final pose; with looping on, the same clip wraps to its own beginning without changing model, state, scene ownership or creating multiple clocks. Seeking/restart clamp to the current clip's range. If Physics is On, preserve existing fixed-step hold, replay, cancellation and device budget behavior; do not modify the numerical Physics model to hide duration problems.
- [ ] Preserve MMD and glTF playback synchronization, IK, Physics On/Off, Toon/PBR, Outline, Expression mode, camera state, single-renderer/resource reuse, loader error/Retry and the newly simplified layout. Keep the downloadable original VMD/metadata unchanged unless correcting a demonstrably inconsistent generated duration field.
- [ ] Avoid introducing external services, arbitrary time padding, an editor-style manual trim option, new limits or assumptions that every clip is 10 s. The principal requirement is to display and obey the authentic per-motion duration.

## Test/verification plan

- [ ] Update public-motion/body-motion browser tests to derive ending seeks and loop thresholds from the **selected validated motion metadata**, rather than `9.9`, `10` or `9`. Include both models and different clips; also assert slider max and total-time label equal the active player's/metadata's duration after each switch.
- [ ] Add a focused controlled non-10-second duration fixture or intercepted validated metadata/player scenario (prefer source-generated synthetic VMD) to prove this is not only coincidentally correct for current 10 s source clips. Test end, loop, clamp, play/pause, restart and accurate label at the final frame; preserve source identity/hash/size checks rather than bypassing them in production. Include fractional frame end.
- [ ] Verify switching from a longer to a shorter clip and back, with Loop enabled and time previously near the old endpoint; verify new range and no stale time in UI or PMX/glTF playback.
- [ ] Verify Rest/initial loading does not show fabricated `10.00 s`, disabled controls remain accessible, and 390px mobile timeline stays usable; neither credits nor Details disclosure is affected.
- [ ] Preserve existing real Uka/Gene performance, source validation, IK and Physics regression checks and test thresholds. Do not weaken assertions just to pass new duration behavior.
- [ ] Run appropriate `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, focused Playwright public-motion/body-motion/UI/Physics cases, `npm run check:links`, `git diff --check`, then required sharded CI on PR. Report actual results, any skips and evidence honestly, keeping the recent CI optimization intact.

## Acceptance

1. **No fixed 10-second assumption** controls the public playback range, initial duration label, end, restart or loop. Any literal 10 in a generic fixture must be explicitly fixture-specific.
2. After selecting any real Uka/Gene clip, slider `max`, current/total display and actual playback duration agree with the selected VMD's canonical metadata/player duration.
3. Multiple different durations (including a non-10 and fractional-frame fixture) exhibit correct endpoint, loop, seek, clamp and handoff behavior; MMD/glTF remain synchronized.
4. The initial loading/Rest interface is honest (no fictional 10-second placeholder), and simplified desktop/mobile controls remain clear.
5. All existing source integrity, IK/Physics, model reuse and browser CI quality requirements continue to pass.

## Workflow

Filed for the designated implementer. The author does not implement, create branches or PRs, or merge. Follow [development-flow.md](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md): default to agent-executable validation; no discretionary human approval/physical-device gate is needed for this duration fix.
